_help: Visual plan for video-03, one entry per script scene (same ids and order as research/video-03/script_v2.json). A scene has parts: one part, or two when the layout changes mid-scene. A part has a type (claim, pair, grid, textcard, rankbars, stack, close) and optional from/to (a cue phrase from the scene's vo_text; default = scene start / scene end). An element with a cue appears at the first exact match of its phrase after the scene start (tools/lib/cue.mjs). An element without a cue is shown from the part start. Text is a string or a list of lines. A number is either a data reference {from, key, field, as, cue} (from: a table name from video.config.json inputs.tables, keyed by that table's key column; as: pct = fmtPct, year = the CSV value; complement = 100 minus the value) or a literal {text, spoken, cue, caption, check}. For every number the cue must equal its spoken form; caption is the number's display in the captions (literal numbers only; data numbers use their on-screen value). A check names a data check in tools/build.mjs. pair: optional subtitle (text, no digits) and title_num (a number, shown at its cue) in the title block; each row has either year (a number) or label {lines, cue?, check?} (text, shown at its cue or at the part start), and a value (a number). close: a block item may carry num (a number, shown at its cue) after its lines. A repeat {prefix, from, key, field, as, repeat_of} shows an earlier number again: repeat_of is the spoken form of that earlier entry, and the build copies its cue and checks the same value shows (build.mjs repeatEl); it has no cue of its own and shows from the part start. A scene may set visual_start_cue (a cue inside that scene): its visuals start there and the previous scene's visuals stay on until then; captions and audio are not affected. The build resolves all times and values; this file holds no timings.
